inventory.rationale: A cancellation snapshot must retain nonzero committed budget state.
A cancellation snapshot must retain nonzero receipt state.
A commit must not mutate budget or receipts while cancellation is pending.
Repeated receipts must not reuse a fixed timestamp.
Receipt creation must advance the logical clock.
Admitting a child at capacity oversubscribes the parent reservation.
Successful completion requires a started dispatch.
Post-dispatch cleanup requires a started dispatch.
The parent receipt may be written only after every child receipt is flushed.
Pre-dispatch cleanup may unwind only an admitted invocation.
Cleanup failures must be limited to resources admitted for the invocation.
Incomplete-stream cleanup requires a started dispatch.
An outcome-unknown server error must retain its monetary hold.
Dispatch may start only from an admitted invocation.
A buffered child count may not exceed the configured capacity.
An allow receipt must be backed by the matching call budget check.
Reproduces registered negative variant receipt-before-allow-guard.
Publishing one allow must not authorize unrelated calls or capabilities.
Every direct parent edge must appear in the descendant closure.
Reproduces registered negative variant revocation-transitive-cut.
Revocation must clear allow eligibility throughout the descendant closure.
A delegated link must retain the parent used to derive its depth.
Every delegation edge must increase depth by exactly one.
Every minted child must preserve its attenuation witness.
A newly minted root must start at depth zero.
A peer may observe only the specific revocation that was issued.
Attenuation may not install a depth beyond the configured ceiling.
Evaluation must never issue allow after observing a revocation epoch.
Propagation must install the signed nonzero revocation epoch.
Installing a revocation epoch must also mark the capability revoked.
A locally revoked capability must enter the revoked state.
A local revocation must record a nonzero observation epoch.
The revocation epoch must be strictly earlier than the next clock value.
